thread:
sandeep: Repro report: long streaming sessions with tool loops show steady memory growth. Repro on staging with ~100k token session, memory climbs ~1.2GB/hour until OOM guard. Running with model=redwood-13b-q, kernel=auto-select, batching off. Attaching perf & heap snippets below.

anna: Can you share the exact run command + env? Also which KV config are you using (slots/eviction)?

sandeep: Run command we used:
```
./perf-run --session-length 100000 --stream --tools=loop.json --model redwood-13b-q --kernel auto
```
KV config: per-session_slots=4096, eviction=LRU, page_size=64kb, kv_reuse=false. Heap snapshot: `heap_dump_1823459999.heap` (uploaded).

chris: Quick profiling notes: jemalloc arenas keep growing (mapped > active), lots of small extents. tl;dr looks like fragmentation rather than live object count. Quick mallctl dump:
```
arenas: 12
active: 3.4GB
mapped: 4.1GB
```
:thinking: allocation histogram shows spike at 4-16KB allocations per token path.

chris: Hypothesis: when kernel=auto selects the per-token optimized matmul path we allocate transient buffers ~6-8KB per token. Over long contexts + tool loops these allocations scatter across arenas and slabs, which combined with pinned KV entries creates fragmentation that never gets returned to OS.

maria: Two quick experiments to try: 1) enable kv_reuse=true (recycle KV slots instead of fresh alloc) and 2) set page_reclaim_interval_ms=500 to force more aggressive page-level reclamation. Can you run A/B with those?

sandeep: Ran with kv_reuse=true + page_reclaim=500. Memory growth slowed (~0.3GB/hr) but didn't stop. After ~12h still creeping; arenas 3 and 5 show most waste. Attached small smaps snippet showing RSS climb.

anna: Can you paste /proc/<pid>/smaps or `pmap -x` output for the process at 3h and 12h marks? Need to see anon vs file-backed and hugepages.

sandeep: Paste (redacted):
```
Rss: 5123456 kB
Pss: 4987123 kB
AnonHugePages: 0 kB
Private_Dirty: 4102344 kB
```
Shows RSS growth primarily in anon memory.

ops-bot: ci/loadtest-longchain #452 finished: mem_growth=+1.1GB/hr (baseline run, kernel=auto, kv_reuse=false) :eyes:

chris: Another angle: eviction policy + tool loops -> tool state pins a bunch of KV entries but access pattern is very sparse and uneven. That creates many partially-used slabs/bins: you can't free a slab if even one live object remains. Solution idea: implement slot compaction/migration pass that relocates live KV entries into dense slots then free empty slabs. Should be incremental to avoid latency spikes.

maria: I'll prototype an incremental compaction pass behind an env var. Plan: compact only when idle OR between tool invocations; yield after X moves to avoid tail latency. Risks: extra CPU and short pauses while copying KV entries (need pointer safety).

sandeep: Sounds good. I'll run extended experiments with kv_reuse + compaction once the patch lands. Also question for chris: can you instrument the kernel allocator path to emit an alloc-size histogram so we can prove the 4-16KB transient alloc hypothesis?

chris: Yep, I can add a simple runtime counter histogram (power-of-two buckets) and expose via /metrics. Will try to get a quick build tonight.

anna: Filing perf issue: #789 - "longchain slot saturation & slab fragmentation". Please drop experiment results there and ping infra when you have the histogram. :thumbsup:

sandeep: Thanks — will update. If compaction + kv_reuse still doesn't fix it, next step is instrumenting per-kernel alloc paths and trying a forced single-arena allocator to see if arena demux is the main culprit.

chris: one more note: check jemalloc tcache flush policy; if tcache keeps small frees local, they may not return to arena quickly. Flushing more aggressively in long runs might help as interim workaround.

maria: Agree. I'll add a config toggle to flush tcache every N tokens for the experiment.

ops-bot: deploy/experimental-compaction scheduled to staging on 1823460500 (auto-notify).

sandeep: Cool — thanks everyone. Keeping this thread for updates.
